estat

Censored-outcome concordance after Cox regression

Stata 

estat concordance

R survival 

survival::concordance(fit)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Censoring weights and handling of tied risks/times affect the statistic.

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Cox proportional-hazards diagnostic

Stata 

estat phtest, detail

R survival 

survival::cox.zph(fit, transform = "identity")

Differs from Stata After the same Cox fit, identity time transform matches the Stata default time scale. Both assess proportional hazards using Schoenfeld residuals. Current survival uses a score-test implementation, so finite-sample statistics can differ from Stata residual-correlation tests.

Stata reference · R reference

predict

Baseline cumulative hazard at zero covariates

Stata 

predict basehaz, basechazard

R survival 

survival::basehaz(fit, centered = FALSE)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Cox baseline is centered at zero explicitly; Stata stores results on observation rows whereas R returns unique event/censoring times.

Stata reference · R reference

Stata 

predict median_time, median

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Distribution-specific predicted survival quantiles; not the mean time.

stci

Restricted mean survival through time nine

Stata 

stci, rmean

R survival 

summary(survival::survfit(s ~ 1), rmean = "common")$table

Differs from Stata rmean="common" restricts the survival integral at the largest observed follow-up time, as Stata stci, rmean does; it does not extrapolate beyond follow-up. Match the analysis sample and censoring declaration.

Stata reference · R reference

stcox

Cox proportional hazards model

Stata 

stcox x1 x2

R survival 

survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, died) ~ x1 + x2, data = data, ties = "breslow")

Differs from Stata Right-censored Cox regression with Breslow ties, matching default stcox. exp(coef(fit)) gives hazard ratios. Assumes one record per subject and positive follow-up.

Cluster-robust Cox inference

Stata 

stcox x z, vce(cluster id) noadjust

R survival 

survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ x + z, ties = "breslow", data = data, cluster = id)

Differs from Stata Breslow Cox model with cluster/sampling-weight sandwich covariance. Stata noadjust disables its default df multiplier to match coxph. Declare probability weights in stset. Require identical complete-data risk sets.

Stata reference · R reference

Cox time-varying log-time coefficient

Stata 

stcox x, tvc(z) texp(ln(_t))

R survival 

survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ x + tt(z), ties = "breslow", data = data, tt = function(z, t, ...) z * log(t))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Match ties, risk intervals, weights and reference inference explicitly.

Stata reference · R reference

Weighted Cox model with sandwich covariance

Stata 

stset time [pw=w], failure(event)
stcox x z, vce(robust) noadjust

R survival 

survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ x + z, ties = "breslow", data = data, weights = w, robust = TRUE)

Differs from Stata Breslow Cox model with cluster/sampling-weight sandwich covariance. Stata noadjust disables its default df multiplier to match coxph. Declare probability weights in stset. Require identical complete-data risk sets.

stgen

Mark subjects ever exposed during their observed survival history

Stata 

stgen ever_x = ever(x==1)

R stats 

transform(data, ever_x = ave(x == 1, id, FUN = function(v) as.integer(any(v))))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. All observed spells contribute to the history. Missing exposure values require an explicit convention rather than treating NA as false.

Stata reference · R reference

stintreg

Lognormal regression for interval-censored outcomes

Stata 

stintreg x, interval(lower upper) distribution(lognormal)

R survival 

survival::survreg(survival::Surv(lower, upper, type = "interval2") ~ x, data = data, dist = "lognormal")

Differs from Stata Stata requires interval(lower upper). The Weibull time option selects AFT coefficients, matching survreg rather than Stata default PH coefficients. For interval2, equal endpoints are exact events, NA lower endpoints denote left censoring, and NA upper endpoints right censoring; encode Stata left-censoring bounds explicitly.

Stata reference · R reference

Differs from Stata Stata requires interval(lower upper). The Weibull time option selects AFT coefficients, matching survreg rather than Stata default PH coefficients. For interval2, equal endpoints are exact events, NA lower endpoints denote left censoring, and NA upper endpoints right censoring; encode Stata left-censoring bounds explicitly.

Parametric survival model

Stata 

streg x, distribution(weibull) time

R survival 

survival::survreg(survival::Surv(time, died) ~ x, data = data, dist = "weibull")

stset

Declare survival-time data

Stata 

stset time, failure(died)

R survival 

survival::Surv(data$time, data$died)

R has no declaration step: Surv(time, died) goes on the left of each model formula.

Stata reference · R reference

Delayed-entry counting-process response

Stata 

stset time, enter(time entry) failure(event)

R survival 

survival::Surv(data$entry, data$time, data$event)

Differs from Stata Surv(entry,time,event) uses (entry,time] counting-process intervals. Match Stata enter(time entry) and use one row per observed risk interval, with event coded 0/1.

Stata reference · R reference

Right-censored survival response

Stata 

stset time, failure(event)

R survival 

survival::Surv(data$time, data$event)

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Creates a response object rather than declaring global dataset state.

Stata reference · R reference

stsplit

Split risk intervals at fixed cut points

Stata 

stsplit period, at(3 6)

R survival 

{ Surv <- survival::Surv; out <- survival::survSplit(Surv(time, event) ~ ., data = data, cut = c(3, 6), start = "start", end = "time", event = "event", episode = "period"); out$period <- c(0, 3, 6)[out$period]; out }

Differs from Stata Zero-entry single-record subjects with an id column. R splits at 3 and 6 and converts the episode index to Stata lower-boundary labels 0,3,6. Events remain on the final risk interval.
